Rashi on Ketubot 72a:10:1.hebrew: דת יהודית - שנהגו בנות ישראל, ואע"ג דלא כתיבא:
Rashi on Ketubot 72a:10:1.english: Jewish practice - [That] which the daughters of Israel practiced, even though it is not written [in the Torah].

Rashi on Ketubot 72a:10:2.english: And [she] spins in the marketplace - [It is] explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Ketubot 72a:10:3.english: [In the case of] one who speaks inside her house - [This] is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Ketubot 72a:11:1.english: What are the circumstances - that she fed him [untithed food].

Rashi on Ketubot 72a:11:2.english: If he knew - when he ate [it].

Rashi on Ketubot 72a:11:3.english: He should abstain - and not eat [it].

Rashi on Ketubot 72a:11:4.english: How does he know - Who told him afterwards, [such] that he comes to divorce her?

Rashi on Ketubot 72a:13:1.hebrew: הוחזקה נדה בשכינותיה - שראוה לובשת בגדי נדות, ולבעלה אמרה "טהורה אני", ושמשה:
Rashi on Ketubot 72a:13:1.english: She was presumed [to be] a menstruant by her neighbors - For they saw her wearing menstrual garments, and to her husband she said, "I am pure," and she cohabited [with him].

Rashi on Ketubot 72a:13:2.hebrew: בעלה לוקה - אם התרו בו. וכי האי גוונא משכחת לה למתני', דלאחר תשמיש הודיעוהו שכינותיו שהוחזקה נדה:
Rashi on Ketubot 72a:13:2.english: Her husband is flogged - [That is,] if they warned him. And in such a case you find [the scenario of] the Mishnah, where after intercourse her neighbors informed him that she was presumed [to be] a menstruant.

Rashi on Ketubot 72a:15:1.hebrew: בנים מתים - בפ' במה מדליקין (שבת לב:) יליף מוחבל את מעשה ידיך:
Rashi on Ketubot 72a:15:1.english: Children die - In the chapter [entitled] Bameh Madlikin (Shabbat 32b), [it] derives [this] from "and destroy the work of your hands" [Ecclesiastes 5:5].

Rashi on Ketubot 72a:16:1.hebrew: ידירנה - משמע בעצמו, קונם עליך דבר פלוני:
Rashi on Ketubot 72a:16:1.english: He should vow [to obligate] her - [This] implies [that he] himself [imposes a vow on her, saying], "Such-and-such a thing is konam [forbidden as a vow] to you."

Rashi on Ketubot 72a:16:2.hebrew: יחזור ויקניטנה - אין לו להוציאה, אלא כך יתקננה:
Rashi on Ketubot 72a:16:2.english: He should return and provoke her - He does not need to divorce her; rather, in this way he will rectify her.

Rashi on Ketubot 72a:16:3.hebrew: בכפיפה - בתוך סל אחד, שכשלא ישמר ישכנו. אף זה יבא לידי שתקלקלנו:
Rashi on Ketubot 72a:16:3.english: In a kefifa - Within a single basket, for when he does not guard himself, it will bite him. So too, this [husband] will come to [a situation] where she ruins him.

Rashi on Ketubot 72a:18:1.hebrew: מאן דמתני לה אהא - דר"י דתני תקנתא אחלה, כל שכן אנדרים דלא שכיחי:
Rashi on Ketubot 72a:18:1.english: He who teaches it with regard to this - [That is,] Rabbi Yehuda, who teaches a remedy for challah, all the more so [would he teach a remedy] for vows, which are not common.

Rashi on Ketubot 72a:19:1.english: It is by Torah [law] - And why does [the Mishnah] not call it the law of Moses?

Rashi on Ketubot 72a:19:2.hebrew: אזהרה - מדעבדינן לה הכי לנוולה, מדה כנגד מדה כמו שעשתה להתנאות על בועלה, מכלל דאסור. א"נ: מדכתיב "ופרע", מכלל דההוא שעתא לאו פרועה הות; שמע מינה אין דרך בנות ישראל לצאת פרועות ראש, וכן עיקר:
Rashi on Ketubot 72a:19:2.english: A warning - Since we do this to her to disgrace her — measure for measure, just as she acted to adorn herself for her paramour — it follows by implication that [going out with an uncovered head] is forbidden. Alternatively: since it is written, "And he shall uncover [the head of the woman]," it follows by implication that at that time she was not uncovered; learn from this that it is not the practice of Jewish women to go out with uncovered heads — and this is the primary [explanation].

Rashi on Ketubot 72a:1:1.english: There is locking in front of her - A door of joy and relief from distress.

Rashi on Ketubot 72a:1:2.hebrew: סופנה - קוברה. כשם שלא גמלה חסד, כך לא יגמלו עמה:
Rashi on Ketubot 72a:1:2.english: Sofnah - Buries her. Just as she did not bestow kindness, so too they will not bestow [kindness] upon her.

Rashi on Ketubot 72a:2:1.hebrew: דיספד - יתן אל לבו שאף הוא יספדוהו, ואל ירע לו אם נהג כן:
Rashi on Ketubot 72a:2:1.english: [He] who eulogizes - He should take to heart that they will also eulogize him, and it should not be grievous to him if he acted thus.

Rashi on Ketubot 72a:2:2.english: [He] who raises [his voice] - He raised his voice in weeping and lamentation.

Rashi on Ketubot 72a:2:3.english: [He] who escorts - [He] escorted the bier from the house of the mourner to the grave.

Rashi on Ketubot 72a:5:1.hebrew: שתהא ממלאה ונופצת - לאחר שתשמש וימלא רחמה שכבת זרע, תרוץ ברגליה ותנפצנו, שלא יקלוט ותתעבר:
Rashi on Ketubot 72a:5:1.english: That she fill and shake [it] out - After she has marital relations and her womb is filled [with] semen, she should run on her feet and shake it out, so that it will not be absorbed and she become pregnant.

Rashi on Ketubot 72a:7:1.english: A mill and an oven - [That are] movable.

Tosafot on Ketubot 72a:11:1.hebrew: אי דידע נפרוש - תימה: דלוקמה כגון דידע ופרש, אבל היא היתה רוצה להאכילו, שלא היתה סבורה שהיה יודע. ואומר ר"י, ד"מאכילתו" משמע שהאכילתו, ומדקדק היאך האכילתו. ומיהו קשה, דדייק נמי הכי א"ולא קוצה לה חלה". ונראה לרשב"א, דמה שרצתה להאכילו אינה יוצאה בלא כתובה, דיכולה לומר: "משחקת הייתי, ואם היית בא לאכול הייתי מונעת אותך":
Tosafot on Ketubot 72a:11:1.english: If he knows, he should abstain - [This is] astonishing: let [the Gemara] establish [the Mishnah] as a case where he knew and abstained, but she wanted to feed him, as she did not think that he knew. And Ri says that "she feeds him" implies that she [actually] fed him, and [the Gemara] asks precisely how she fed him. However, [this is] difficult, for [the Gemara] also infers this very thing regarding "[and she] does not separate challah for it." And it appears to Rashba that for [merely] wanting to feed him, she does not leave without [her] ketubah, for she can say: "I was joking, and if you had come to eat, I would have prevented you."

Tosafot on Ketubot 72a:11:2.hebrew: פלוני כהן תיקן כו' - היה יכול לומר דאיכא עדים שהאכילתו דבר שאינו מעושר, אלא לא שכיח:
Tosafot on Ketubot 72a:11:2.english: "So-and-so the priest rectified, etc." - [The Gemara] could have said that there are witnesses that she fed him something that was not tithed, except that [such a case] is not common.

Tosafot on Ketubot 72a:12:1.hebrew: אי דלא ידע נסמוך עילוה - הכא לא מצי לאקשויי "אי דלא ידע מנא ידע?" כדפריך לעיל, שהרי יכול לדעת שראה בגדיה אחרי כן מלוכלכים בדם; להכי פריך "נסמוך עילוה", שאומרת שנתלכלכו לה ממקום אחר:
Tosafot on Ketubot 72a:12:1.english: If he does not know, he should rely on her - Here [the Gemara] cannot ask, "If he does not know, how would he know?" as it asked above, because he can know, since he saw her garments stained with blood afterward; therefore it asks, "[Why not] rely on her," when she says that they became stained from another source.

Tosafot on Ketubot 72a:12:2.hebrew: וספרה לה לעצמה - וא"ת: אמאי אין מברכת זבה על ספירתה כמו שמברכין על ספירת העומר, דהא כתיב "וספרה"? וי"ל: דאין מברכין אלא ביובל, שמברכין ב"ד בכל שנה, שלעולם יוכל למנות כסדר, וכן עומר; אבל זבה, שאם תראה תסתור — אין לה למנות:
Tosafot on Ketubot 72a:12:2.english: "Then she shall count to herself" — "by herself": And if you ask: Why does a zavah not recite a blessing over her counting, just as we recite a blessing over the counting of the Omer, since it is written, "and she shall count"? One can answer that one only recites a blessing [in cases like] the Jubilee, where the court recites a blessing each year, because one can always count in sequence — and similarly [for the] Omer; whereas a zavah, who if she sees [blood] will forfeit [her count], does not [recite a blessing] to count.

Tosafot on Ketubot 72a:16:1.hebrew: יחזור ויקניטנה כדי שתדור בפניו ויפר לה - ואם לא שיקניטנה, לא ידע מתי תדור שיפר. ואע"ג דבעיא היא בפ' נערה המאורסה (נדרים דף עב:) אם בעל מיפר בלא שמיעה או לא — לא שיוכל להפר נדרים שתדור מכאן ולהבא, דאם כן תפשוט מהכא דאין מיפר בלא שמיעה מדמצריך להקניטה; אלא מיירי בנדרים שכבר נדרה ולא שמע, אבל הכא היכי יפר? דשמא עדיין לא נדרה, ולאחר מיכן שמא תדור ותעבור מיד קודם שיפר. והא דבעי למפשט מדתניא: "האומר לאשתו כל נדרים שתדור מכאן עד שאבא ממקום פלוני הרי הן מופרין, ר"א אומר: מופר" — לא משום דמיבעיא ליה היכא דלא נדרה; תדע, מדפשיט מדר"א, ואדרבה מדרבנן הו"ל למפשט דקתני: "וחכ"א: אינו מופר"! אלא ה"ק התם: מדר"א נשמע לרבנן, דע"כ לא פליגי עליה רבנן אלא בהא דאין יכול להפר קודם שיחול הנדר, אבל בהא מודו רבנן דאם כבר חל הנדר דמיפר אע"ג דלא שמע:
Tosafot on Ketubot 72a:16:1.english: He should return and provoke her, so that she will vow in his presence and he can nullify [it] for her - And if he does not provoke her, he will not know when she vows so that he can nullify [it]. And even though it is an unresolved question in the chapter [entitled] Na'arah HaMe'orasah (Nedarim 72b) whether a husband can nullify [a vow] without hearing [it] or not — [that question is] not whether he can nullify vows that she will vow from now on, for if so, you could resolve from here that he cannot nullify without hearing, since [the baraita] requires him to provoke her; rather, [that question] refers to vows that she has already vowed and he has not heard; but here, how could he nullify [them]? For perhaps she has not yet vowed, and afterward she might vow and immediately transgress [the vow] before he nullifies [it]. And [as for] that which [the Gemara there] seeks to resolve [the question] from what was taught [in a baraita]: "One who says to his wife, 'All vows that you will vow from now until I return from such-and-such a place, behold, they are nullified,' Rabbi Eliezer says: It is nullified" — [this is] not because it was a question to him where she has not [yet] vowed; know [that this is so] from the fact that [the Gemara] resolves [it] from Rabbi Eliezer, whereas on the contrary, it should have resolved [it] from the Rabbis, as [the baraita] teaches: "And the Sages say: It is not nullified"! Rather, this is what [the Gemara] is saying there: From Rabbi Eliezer we may infer regarding the Rabbis, for the Rabbis only disagree with him in this [respect], that he cannot nullify before the vow takes effect, but in this [respect] the Rabbis agree that if the vow has already taken effect, he can nullify [it] even though he has not heard [it].

Tosafot on Ketubot 72a:8:1.hebrew: המדיר את אשתו שלא תשאל כו' - תימה, דעל כרחך לא מיירי הכא בנדרה היא וקיים לה הוא, דהא קתני סיפא: "וכן היא שנדרה"; ואיהו לא מצי לאדורה אא"כ תלה בתשמיש. וא"כ לשמואל, למה יוציא לאלתר, ותשאל ותיאסר לב"ה שבת אחת? וי"ל, דלעולם שלא תלה בתשמיש, אלא כגון שאסר על עצמו הנאת שאילתה ואינה יכולה בשביל זה לשאל, ולא תשאיל — שאסר הנאת כליו שלא תוכל להשאילם:
Tosafot on Ketubot 72a:8:1.english: "One who vows [and obligates] his wife not to borrow, etc." - This is perplexing, for perforce [it] is not dealing here with [a case where] she vowed and he upheld [the vow] for her, since the latter clause teaches: "And similarly, [if it is] she who vowed." And he cannot impose a vow upon her unless he made [it] contingent upon marital relations. And if so, according to Shmuel, why must he divorce [her] immediately, rather than let her borrow and be forbidden [from marital relations for] one week according to Beit Hillel? And it can be answered that in fact [it is a case] where he did not make [it] contingent upon marital relations, rather, for example, where he forbade upon himself the benefit of her borrowing, and because of this she cannot borrow; and "not to lend" — [meaning] that he forbade the benefit of his utensils so that she cannot lend them.
